org.name: St. Anne's Episcopal Church
org.tagline: A parish in downtown Longmont since 1892
org.mission: St. Anne's is a liturgical parish: sung services, the old prayers, a choir that rehearses on Thursdays, and a stone church that has stood at Fourth and Coffman since 1892. We keep the doors open all week, run a preschool in the parish hall, and walk the labyrinth on the first Friday of every month.
org.about:
The stone church at Fourth and Coffman was consecrated in 1892, when Longmont was a sugar-beet town. The nave seats two hundred and forty; on Easter it holds more.

There are three services every Sunday. The eight o'clock is spoken and quiet, the ten-fifteen has the choir and the organ, and the five o'clock is a shorter said Eucharist for people who work weekends. Choral Evensong is sung on the last Sunday of the month at four.

The parish hall is home to St. Anne's Preschool on weekday mornings, forty-two children this year. The labyrinth in the garden is open to anyone, any time; on first Fridays we light it with candles.

About three hundred people call St. Anne's their parish. Many have for decades; some found it last month.

testimonials.quote: I'm not sure what I believe, but I come for Evensong every month and sit near the back. Nobody has ever asked me to be anything else.

testimonials.quote: Our daughter did two years at the preschool. She still calls the labyrinth 'the maze that isn't a maze.'

posts.title: The organ restoration is finished
posts.body:
After fourteen months, the 1911 Kimball is back in the loft. The pipes have been cleaned and revoiced, the bellows releathered, and the swell box works for the first time in living memory.

You will hear it at the ten-fifteen on September 14th. A dedication recital follows at three; everyone is welcome and there is no charge.

posts.title: Preschool enrollment for January
posts.body:
St. Anne's Preschool has four places opening in January for children aged three to five. Mornings, 8:30 to 12:30, in the parish hall.

Come to the open morning on October 9th, or call the office to arrange a visit.

events.title: Blessing of the Animals
events.description: The feast of St. Francis. Bring dogs on leads, cats in carriers, and anything else that will sit still. The service is outdoors, weather permitting.

notes: We are Episcopal, not Catholic; please don't call the priest 'Father' on the site. Her name is the Rev. Claire Whitfield.
